trust_decision.summary: Whether XML handed to Jackrabbit's DOM builders (privilege definitions, node type definitions, XML-persisted item state) may declare DTDs / resolve external entities; decided only by the default JAXP factory settings in PrivilegeXmlHandler.createFactory/createDocumentBuilder and the DOMWalker static factory, which set no XXE features and no entity resolver.

landing_point.why: The advisory describes blind XXE from an insecure document build when loading privileges; PrivilegeXmlHandler is the privilege XML parser and its createFactory is the obvious DocumentBuilderFactory.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API new PrivilegeDefinitionReader(InputStream|Reader, "text/xml") (PrivilegeDefinitionReader.java:47,69); used by PrivilegeRegistry custom privilege store load/append and cluster journal AbstractRecord.readPrivilegeDef
same as above (createDocumentBuilder used by readDefinitions at PrivilegeXmlHandler.java:161)

public API NodeTypeManagerImpl.registerNodeTypes(InputStream, "text/xml") -> NodeTypeReader -> DOMWalker (NodeTypeManagerImpl.java:239-242, NodeTypeReader.java:108); also NodeTypeDefStore.load and XMLPersistenceManager load
fix_sites.module_kind: internal utility in repository core (jackrabbit-core util)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: jackrabbit-core/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/core/util/DOMWalker.java:40-61 (separate DOM-building helper in another module, reached by node type XML registration jackrabbit-core/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/core/nodetype/NodeTypeManagerImpl.java:239-242 and XML persistence jackrabbit-core/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/core/persistence/xml/XMLPersistenceManager.java:473)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about privilege loading; DOMWalker is a generic core utility used for node type definitions and on-disk persistence files that only admins/the repository write, so a solver can argue it is a different feature and trusted input.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Repository/workspace configuration and indexing configuration files carry a DOCTYPE with public/system IDs resolved to bundled DTDs by custom entity resolvers; an over-broad fix (a shared hardened factory, global disallow-doctype-decl or a JAXP system property) breaks repository startup. Also NodeTypeReader must still read xmlns namespace declarations through DOMWalker.

external general entity, external parameter entity / external DTD load, XInclude (fix.diff:37-54, fix.diff:106-123)

O7_producer.where: jackrabbit-core/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/core/journal/AbstractRecord.java:178 (writes privilege XML into cluster journal) read back at jackrabbit-core/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/core/journal/AbstractRecord.java:304-307; custom_privileges.xml written at jackrabbit-core/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/core/security/authorization/PrivilegeRegistry.java:1131-1133 and re-parsed at :1085-1087, :1107-1109

O8_uncovered_routes.route: jcr2spi (second JCR implementation) Session.importXML parses user XML with a default SAXParserFactory and an ImportHandler that extends DefaultHandler without overriding resolveEntity, so external entities resolve by default; core's equivalent goes through ParsingContentHandler, whose resolveEntity returns empty input.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Content import (system/document view) is a different feature from privilege/node type document builds, it sits in the client-side SPI bridge, and core's importXML is already protected.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module (jackrabbit-jcr2spi) and package from both fix sites

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SAX XMLReaderFactory.createXMLReader() with no entity resolver or features parsing a named file; real at the pinned commit, could be framed as a tooling helper reached by a namespace-import route.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A tooling helper for CND writers; a maintainer would see it as dev-only and never harden it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: node type definitions in the cluster journal read back through an XML reader (currently CND) — an XML variant through DOMWalker or a local factory would be a natural serialization-boundary sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Privilege defs already cross the journal as XML (AbstractRecord.java:304-307); doing the same for node types is a plausible design.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a custom factory passed to setFactory skips the default entity resolver; a planted caller that injects a plain factory would be a realistic how-type sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The public setter exists for customization and skips the resolver by design.

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module (Java 8+); dependencies must be fetched once
O10_build.project_tests: jackrabbit-core/src/test/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/core/util/DOMWalkerTest.java; jackrabbit-spi-commons/src/test/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/spi/commons/privilege/PrivilegeHandlerTest.java (readtest.xml/writetest.xml); node type XML tests in jackrabbit-core

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Harden only PrivilegeXmlHandler.createFactory (the privilege parser the advisory names), leaving DOMWalker in jackrabbit-core and the jcr2spi import parser open.

out_of_scope_notes: DavDocumentBuilderFactory only sets FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and drops its entity resolver when a custom factory is set (jackrabbit-webdav/src/main/java/org/apache/jackrabbit/webdav/xml/DavDocumentBuilderFactory.java:49-55,80-83); not part of this advisory.
